title: Post-launch metrics dashboard plan — Latency/$ benchmark report
content:
Purpose
Track whether the public Latency/$ benchmark report is (1) generating qualified demand and (2) moving active evaluations forward, with enough segmentation to answer “what worked” and “what to do next” (refresh cadence, channel mix, CTA changes).

Owners
- Metrics/attribution: Tyler Benson (Mops)
- Datasets & reporting tables: Mei Lin (Analytics)
- Pipeline reporting + stage definitions: Isabelle Laurent (Sales Ops)
- Campaign execution + readout owner: Ben Carter (Growth)
- SDR execution + meeting booked definitions: Grace O’Connor + Rohan Mehta
- CS follow-up signals: Jasmine Liu

Primary questions this dashboard must answer
1) Did the report drive incremental high-intent traffic (vs baseline)?
2) Did visitors actually consume the content (downloads, time, scroll, methodology clicks)?
3) Did consumption convert to actions (signups, console usage, “talk to us” requests, meetings booked)?
4) Did actions become pipeline (new opps) and influence pipeline (touchpoints on existing opps)?
5) Which channels, regions, and personas performed best (and where did we see “tourists”)?

Time windows (standard views)
- Launch week: Day 0 to Day +7
- Launch month: Day 0 to Day +30
- Baseline comparison: trailing 4-week average pre-launch (excluding holidays) + YoY where available
- Long tail: Day +31 to Day +90 (content compounding)

Key assets in scope (landing + report + supporting pages)
- Benchmark landing page (primary)
- PDF download endpoint (primary)
- Methodology appendix page (secondary credibility driver)
- Launch blog post (secondary)
- Docs cross-links (SDK quickstart mentions + region header clarification)

Dashboard structure (v1)
A) Executive summary (one screen)
- Total sessions to landing page (LP)
- Unique visitors to LP
- Report downloads (unique) + download rate
- Net new signups attributed (first-touch + lead-creation touch)
- Meetings booked attributed (SDR/AEs)
- New pipeline created (amount + count)
- Pipeline influenced (amount + count; defined below)
- Top 3 channels by (a) downloads and (b) pipeline created

B) Web funnel (behavioral)
Funnel steps (all should be filterable by channel/region)
1. Landing page view
2. “Download PDF” click
3. Download success (thank-you or file fetch event)
4. CTA click(s): “Start for free”, “Talk to an expert”, “See pricing”, “Reproduce this benchmark”
5. Signup start
6. Signup complete
7. First key product event (see PLG activation)

Core web metrics
- Sessions, users, engaged sessions
- Bounce rate (or engaged-session rate depending on analytics platform)
- Avg engagement time (or time on page)
- Scroll depth (25/50/75/90%)
- Outbound clicks to docs/github (reproduction example)

Recommended charts
- Daily time series (Day -14 to Day +30) for sessions + downloads + signups
- Funnel conversion rates with confidence intervals (note: low N early days)
- Channel x conversion heatmap (e.g., “download rate” and “signup rate”)

C) Acquisition & channel performance
Breakdowns
- Channel group: organic search, paid search, paid social, organic social, email, partner, direct, referral
- Campaign: UTM campaign name
- Source/medium
- Content: social angle / email variant (utm_content)

Success criteria (tentative; align in PM-445 readout)
- Focus on: download rate, meeting-booked rate, and opp conversion (not just traffic)
- “Quality” proxy: % of downloads that lead to (a) signup+activation or (b) meeting booked within 14 days

D) PLG activation and product usage (post-signup)
Goal: separate “report tourists” from teams actually evaluating inference.

Cohort definition: Report-driven signups
A user/account is “report-driven” if any of the following is true within attribution windows:
- First-touch session has utm_campaign in {benchmark_report_2025Q1, latency_per_dollar_report, …}
- Last-touch before signup complete has the above utm_campaign
- Lead/source in CRM is “Benchmark report” (explicit form field) OR referrer contains /benchmark (LP)

Activation events (first 7 days post-signup)
- Created API key
- First successful inference call (hosted)
- First streaming request
- First embeddings call
- Viewed usage analytics page (console)
- Added payment method OR requested Dedicated/Private info

Activation metrics
- Signup → API key created (rate + median time)
- Signup → first inference (rate + median time)
- % reaching “2+ inference days” in first 14 days (stickiness proxy)
- Cost/usage: total tokens generated in first 14 days (bucketed; do not expose customer-level)

E) Sales outcomes (meetings + pipeline)
Definitions (align with Sales Ops)
- Meeting booked: meeting scheduled in CRM with Meeting Type in {Discovery, Technical evaluation, Dedicated/Private consult} AND source campaign = benchmark OR meeting description includes tracking token.
- New opportunity created: Opp created within 30 days of first report touch, where primary campaign source = benchmark OR first-touch = benchmark.
- Pipeline created: Sum of Amount for “New opportunities created” (above).
- Pipeline influenced: Opps that had ANY benchmark touchpoint (page view, download, email click, meeting where report shared) during the opp lifecycle, even if sourced elsewhere.

Influence model (v1; keep it simple)
- 1) Sourced pipeline: first-touch OR lead-creation touch.
- 2) Influenced pipeline: any touch in the 90 days prior to close date OR between opp create and close.
- Report both; do not mix.

Sales funnel metrics (for sourced opps)
- Opp created → Stage 2 (rate)
- Stage 2 → Stage 3 (rate)
- Win rate (early proxy; may be too soon for launch month)
- Sales cycle length (median; likely only available later)

F) Region + segment views (for messaging and prioritization)
Filters
- Geography: inferred from IP at first session + declared billing country + requested region
- Region interest: if user selected region header or visited region docs pages
- Company segment: employee bucket (CRM enrichment), or self-serve vs sales-assisted
- Industry: if available via enrichment; otherwise “unknown”

Why this matters
- The report is explicitly per cloud region; we need to see if EU/APAC traffic actually converts and whether data residency messaging is doing its job.

Event instrumentation & data sources
Web analytics
- Source: GA4 (or equivalent) + Segment (if used) to warehouse
- Required events
  - page_view (already)
  - benchmark_download_click
  - benchmark_download_success (preferred: fire on thank-you page load or file fetch callback)
  - benchmark_methodology_click
  - benchmark_cta_click (with cta_type)
  - scroll_depth (if available)
- Required parameters
  - page_path, page_title
  - utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign, utm_content, utm_term
  - region_selector_value (if user toggles region on page)

Product analytics
- Source: Redwood Console events → warehouse
- Key events: api_key_created, inference_request_succeeded, embeddings_request_succeeded, payment_method_added, contact_sales_submitted
- Join keys: user_id, account_id; map to CRM where possible.

CRM
- Source: HubSpot (leads/contacts) + Salesforce (opps) depending on current system of record (confirm exact routing)
- Required fields
  - Original source, latest source
  - Campaign association (benchmark campaign)
  - Meeting scheduled date, meeting type, outcome
  - Opp stage, amount, create date, close date
  - Region requirement (free-text is okay; add structured field if possible)

Warehouse / BI
- Source of truth: analytics warehouse tables (Mei Lin)
- BI tool: Looker/Mode (confirm)

Attribution standards (to avoid future arguments)
- Use UTMs for channel/campaign reporting.
- Use explicit campaign association in CRM for sales reporting.
- Do not claim causality; present “sourced” and “influenced” separately.
- Always include a baseline comparison.

Cohorts (standard)
C0 — All visitors
C1 — Engaged visitors: spent >30s OR scrolled >50% OR clicked methodology
C2 — Downloaders
C3 — Signup starters
C4 — Signup completes
C5 — Activated (any activation event in 7 days)
C6 — Sales-intent: contact sales submitted OR meeting booked
C7 — Sourced pipeline

Required slices (apply to cohorts)
- Channel group
- Region (NA/EU/APAC) based on first touch
- Company size bucket (enriched)
- Buyer type proxy
  - Developer: visited docs/repro pages, signed up self-serve
  - Enterprise/security: visited security/compliance pages, requested Dedicated/Private

Data QA checklist (must pass before launch week ends)
1) UTM propagation works from landing page to signup complete.
2) Download success is tracked (not just click).
3) Email links use consistent utm_campaign + utm_content.
4) Paid social links use consistent utm_campaign + utm_content.
5) Partner links use partner-specific utm_source and utm_campaign.
6) “Book a meeting” flows create a campaign association in CRM.
7) Internal traffic excluded (Redwood employees).
8) Bot filtering applied (at least via GA4 default + sanity thresholds).

UTM naming conventions (lock this)
- utm_campaign: benchmark_report_2025q1 (lowercase)
- utm_source: linkedin | x | email | partner_{name} | google
- utm_medium: paid_social | organic_social | email | referral | cpc
- utm_content: angle_latency_per_dollar | angle_methodology | angle_region_eu | angle_embeddings
- utm_term: optional for paid search keywords

Reporting cadence
- Daily (launch week): traffic, downloads, errors, top channels (Tyler)
- Weekly (first month): funnel + early activation + meetings (Tyler + Mei)
- Monthly (through Day +90): sourced/influenced pipeline updates (Isabelle)

Deliverables
1) “Benchmark Launch Dashboard (v1)” in BI tool
- Tabs: Exec, Web funnel, Channel, PLG activation, Sales impact, Region/Segment
2) Readout template (1–2 pages)
- What happened, why, what we change next
3) Data dictionary (appendix)
- Event names, definitions, joins, caveats

Risks / known gaps
- Pipeline influence is inherently messy; keep it conservative and transparent.
- Long sales cycles mean pipeline created/influenced will lag; do not over-index on Day +30.
- If download is cached/CDN-served, ensure download_success still triggers reliably.

Next steps
- Tyler: finalize UTM matrix + update all channel asset links (due: 2025-02-03)
- Mei: confirm warehouse tables + draft Looker explores (due: 2025-02-05)
- Isabelle: lock sourced vs influenced definitions + CRM campaign mapping (due: 2025-02-06)
- Ben: confirm which KPIs go into the executive summary (due: 2025-02-06)

Open questions
- Which system is source-of-truth for meetings booked this quarter (HubSpot vs Salesforce activity sync)?
- Are we comfortable defining “activation” as first successful inference call, or do we require a minimum token threshold?
- Do we want a separate cohort for Dedicated/Private interest (security page views, region residency pages, contact sales) vs Hosted API self-serve?
